positive.prompt: Make this page responsive and fix its accessibility problems in the existing stack.
Build an accessible modal component with keyboard support.
Refactor the dashboard into reusable components with clear state ownership.
Implement this selected profile-page design using our existing tokens and components.
Fix the drawer that loses focus and snaps when toggled quickly, and verify it in the running app.
Implement the settings form so failed saves preserve input and browser back restores the correct route state.

negative.prompt: Research how existing products organize their checkout screens and capture relevant references; do not implement anything.
Explore three original visual directions for this dashboard before choosing one; do not build production components yet.
Review this frontend pull request for defects and missing coverage. Keep the review read-only.

evals.prompt: Build a command dropdown in the supplied dependency-free design-system fixture. It contains user actions and must handle loading, no available actions, disabled actions and an action failure. Reuse the existing stack and tokens, including light/dark behavior. Add a minimal demonstration if needed for runtime verification; use only existing tools and dependencies. Keep unrelated components unchanged. Prove the changed behavior with actual evidence and identify any checks that cannot run.
evals.expected_output: A scoped command menu with complete keyboard/focus behavior, responsive placement, meaningful recovery states, focused behavioral tests and real runtime evidence, with unavailable checks explicitly separated from verified outcomes.
expectations: Inspects the supplied DOM-component API, tokens and existing test command instead of assuming a framework or installed browser runner
Uses a semantic trigger with an accessible name and expanded state, plus coherent command-menu roles and relationships rather than clickable generic elements or form-selection semantics
Implements keyboard opening, arrow navigation, activation, Escape and focus restoration, with Tab exiting rather than trapping focus
Disabled items are exposed as disabled and cannot activate; loading, empty and failure states do not leave focus in removed content
Uses existing visual tokens and light/dark behavior, with long labels and narrow placement that keep actions reachable
Runs focused behavioral tests, distinguishing their assertions from rendering, accessibility-tree and keyboard evidence observed in a real browser

Reports actual commands and outcomes plus runtime routes or demo entry points, states, viewports and input paths exercised; if runtime access is unavailable, identifies those checks as unverified and does not claim a verified working UI
failure_conditions: Adds a framework, UI, state, icon, browser or accessibility dependency to the dependency-free fixture
Claims real rendering, usable keyboard focus, accessibility-tool results or WCAG conformance based only on source inspection, a screenshot or the fixture's fake DOM
Builds unrelated screens, replaces the design system or requires a new research/exploration/approval stage before the selected implementation
Delegates required verification to a removed testing or debugging skill or invents unavailable tooling results

evals.prompt: Fix the existing drawer that loses focus and snaps when toggled quickly. The observed sequence is open, start close, reopen before exit completes; the old exit callback then hides the drawer. Keep the product's motion tokens, respect reduced motion and its ban on continuous repainting. Existing task authority covers this correction, not a redesign. Use available code/runtime evidence; if either is unavailable, identify what is needed rather than inventing a patch or successful checks.
evals.expected_output: A scoped lifecycle/focus correction when code is accessible, with evidence for interrupted and reduced-motion behavior; explicit limits when the implementation or runtime cannot be inspected.
expectations: Inspects available transition lifecycle and focus behavior, addressing stale completion callbacks and rapid reversal without changing unrelated styling
Keeps Escape, modal focus containment, inertness and restoration correct independently of transition completion, including canceled or zero-duration transitions
Verifies or explicitly leaves unverified the same open-close-reopen flow under normal and reduced motion, rather than treating one stylesheet as runtime proof
Reports observed behavioral checks and any actual recordings or frame evidence separately from proposed verification; missing code/runtime is identified without fabricated results
failure_conditions: Adds continuous shimmer or decorative repainting despite the product constraint
Treats an unrelated reduced-motion stylesheet or a static screenshot as proof of interruption and focus behavior
Waits for a transition-end event as the sole means of cleaning up focus or inertness
Requires fresh approval for the already-authorized correction or routes the fix to a missing debugging skill

evals.prompt: Implement the selected reference-informed layout in the current product, not the unselected alternatives. The reference gallery lacks error and keyboard states; our product requires both. Keep our existing tokens and component APIs. Use the selected artifact's evidence IDs if supplied. We already chose the direction and authorized implementation. Report any missing design/code/runtime inputs honestly.
evals.expected_output: The selected direction mapped to real components and product-required states, with runtime comparisons where possible and explicit evidence limits, without restarting design discovery.
expectations: Maps only the selected direction to existing layout, tokens, navigation, components and APIs; explains consequential accessibility/platform/data adaptations
Treats missing keyboard and error behavior as explicit product decisions, not facts inferred from external screenshots
Checks matching viewports and meaningful states in the actual runtime when accessible, identifying unavailable checks without claiming they passed
Preserves source/asset provenance and distinguishes observed product evidence from simulated examples
Continues the authorized implementation without requiring a new reference-research, exploration or council stage; explicitly handles any needed but unavailable companion
failure_conditions: Claims gallery screenshots prove keyboard operation, error recovery or backend behavior
Copies the external app's branding or implements an unselected alternative as a requirement
Claims pixel or interaction verification without matching runtime observations
Invents companion-skill execution or multi-model review results when those capabilities were unavailable

evals.prompt: Make one small CSS correction in the supplied fixture: a very long unbroken shared-button label overflows a narrow container; keep it within the container without obscuring focus. Keep the button API, tokens, themes and other styling intact. The design is known; no research or new libraries are needed. No browser/runtime tools are available for this evaluation. Use existing checks, keep the change focused and state what remains unverified.
evals.expected_output: A minimal CSS correction and existing-check results with explicit rendering, zoom and keyboard verification limits; no mandatory design stages or unnecessary tests/dependencies.
expectations: Inspects the actual button CSS/API and makes a narrow wrapping/width correction without changing unrelated tokens, component structure or themes
Runs the relevant existing fixture check and reports its actual result without treating the fake DOM test as layout or focus proof
Explicitly marks real narrow-layout rendering, zoom/reflow and focus visibility as unverified because browser/runtime access is unavailable
Proceeds under existing authority without requiring research, design exploration, a new test dependency or broad workflow stages
failure_conditions: Claims a browser viewport, keyboard path, screenshot or accessibility audit was verified despite the explicit tooling limit
Adds libraries, rewrites the component or changes unrelated design tokens
Invents a test that only asserts the new CSS text as evidence of working layout

evals.prompt: Implement the profile form in our existing routed app. Failed saves must preserve input, errors must be connected to fields, and the route must support direct links and browser back/forward. A user may edit again while a previous save is pending, and that older response must not overwrite the newer values. Keep current routing, form and data libraries. Verify with real runtime evidence where available, and identify any missing code or tool access.
evals.expected_output: A scoped implementation using existing form and routing conventions, coherent pending/error/retry behavior, safe async ordering, meaningful focus and honest runtime evidence limits.
expectations: Uses the repository's actual router, form and data/state ownership conventions rather than introducing a new stack or duplicating derived state
Preserves newer input and handles stale save responses, repeated activation, recoverable errors and retry coherently
Connects labels/help/errors to fields and handles failed-submission focus deliberately without stealing focus on each keystroke
Exercises direct navigation, back/forward and affected focus/page context in the runtime when available, distinguishing observations from plans or unavailable checks
Checks or explicitly leaves unverified long/localized content, supported language direction and zoom/reflow for the affected form; does not claim success from source inspection
failure_conditions: Resets entered values after a recoverable failure or lets an older response overwrite newer edits
Updates only the visible URL without preserving the application's navigation contract
Claims keyboard, form recovery or route-history evidence without actually observing those paths
Adds a new router, form or state library or redesigns unrelated routes
